## Findings
- claim-1: The supplied record states that Theorem 5.4 gives two generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) and records \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6@L14-L33|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: For \((r,q,i,j)=(2,6,1,1)\) and \((5,2,1,1)\), one has \(a=b=1\), hence \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}=2\). The two prescribed families specialize respectively to \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(2)}\}\) and \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(1,1)}\}\).
- claim-3: In the standard integral Grassmannian quotient \(A\) for either \(2^6\) or \(6^2\), \(A\) is generated by \(h_1,h_2\), and \[ A_+=(h_1,h_2),\qquad A_+/A_+^2\cong\mathbb Z\bar h_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar h_2. \] Indeed, for \(q=2\), \(h_k=0\) for \(k>2\). For \(r=2\), \(e_k=0\) for \(k>2\), so \(h_m=e_1h_{m-1}-e_2h_{m-2}\), with \(e_1=h_1\) and \(e_2=h_1^2-h_2\). In degree \(2\), \(A_2\) has basis \(s_{(2)},s_{(1,1)}\), while \((A_+^2)_2=\mathbb Z(s_{(2)}+s_{(1,1)})\).
- claim-4: Assuming the Theorem-5.4 generation assertion for these specialized families, both displayed two-element sets are minimal generating sets for \(J_{v_{2,2,2,8}}\) and \(J_{v_{5,5,5,7}}\). The first set is \(\{h_1,h_2\}\), hence generates \(A_+\) and therefore \(J_v=A_+\). The second is \(\{h_1,e_2\}\), and \(e_2=h_1^2-h_2\), so it generates the same ideal. Modulo \(A_+^2\), its images are \((\bar h_1,-\bar h_2)\); thus each pair is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J_v/A_+J_v\), so neither member is deletable.
## Strategy
For each tuple use
\[
t=r-j+1,\quad s=i+r-j,\quad n=r+q,
\]
giving respectively \(v_{2,2,2,8}\) and \(v_{5,5,5,7}\). In both cases \(a=b=1\), so the two reported Theorem-5.4 families are
\[
\{s_{(1)},s_{(2)}\}=\{h_1,h_2\},\qquad
\{s_{(1)},s_{(1,1)}\}=\{h_1,e_2\}.
\]
Treat both families for each permutation.

In the Grassmannian quotients for \(6^2\) and \(2^5\), prove \(A_+=(h_1,h_2)\). Since \(A\) is generated by \(h_1,h_2\), every homogeneous element of degree at least \(2\) lies in \(A_+^2\). Thus
\[
A_+/A_+^2\cong \mathbb Z[h_1]\oplus\mathbb Z[h_2],
\]
where the degree-two assertion uses
\[
(A_+^2)_2=\mathbb Z(h_1^2)
=\mathbb Z(s_{(2)}+s_{(1,1)}),
\]
so \(A_2/(A_+^2)_2\cong\mathbb Z\), without torsion. The two pairs induce bases \((h_1,h_2)\) and \((h_1,-h_2)\), respectively, because \(e_2=h_1^2-h_2\).

Subject to the reported generation assertion in ledger claim-1, each pair generates \(A_+\), hence \(J_v=A_+\) and \(A_+J_v=A_+^2\). The indexed graded Nakayama criterion then proves irredundance.

## Gaps
The generation assertion is grounded only by the validated ordinary-document record, not a directly supplied formal statement of Theorem 5.4. Therefore the final minimality certification remains conditional on that assertion.
